item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E002","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Scholz said Germany would supply Ukraine with heavy weapons, including Leopard 2 tanks, while coordinating with allies, and that Germany would provide training, logistics, ammunition, and maintenance; he framed the policy as supporting Ukraine's defence while preventing escalation into a NATO-Russia war and said decisions were taken incrementally because there were no mathematically certain choices.","notes":["Training of Ukrainian crews was stated conditionally, so the summary was narrowed to Germany providing training generally."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E003","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E005","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E006","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Scholz stated that Germany had created a €100 billion Bundeswehr special fund through an amendment to the Basic Law, intended to build military capability, and committed to permanently spending 2% of GDP on defence; he also described NATO readiness, additional deployments for Lithuania, air-defence assistance to Poland and Slovakia, and protection of North and Baltic Sea infrastructure.","notes":["The excerpt says the amendment had support from the largest opposition party, not specifically that it was enacted by a parliamentary majority."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E009","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E010","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E011","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"During the same 29 March questioning, Scholz said the child supplement was received by about 30% of lower-income families, compared with 100% uptake of child benefit, and said the government needed to increase that share;
